# Set-up

### Set WD for knitr
Manually setWD to "......./Data Package/Study 1"
```{r setup, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
require("knitr")
opts_knit$set(root.dir = "~/How Hwee/PhD Stuff/Research/Self-Punishment/Data Package/Study 1")
```

### Load packages
```{r message=F}
library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
library(effsize)
library(tidyr)
library(emmeans)
library(car)
library(ggpubr)
library(WRS2)
```

### Read data file
- Because participants' age can be potentially identifiable (e.g., several participants have idiosyncratic ages; 51), I have separated that into a standalone file (where age is sorted in ascending order) to prevent matching of age and responses on main dataset. 
- We had excluded two participants from analyses for failing comprehension checks. Their ages were manually removed from the age file. There was 1 missing response for age. 
- This resulted in 273 valid responses (276 - 2 - 1 = 273)
```{r}
# Read CSV
df <- read.csv("Data Files/Study 1 - Raw Data - Deidentified.csv", skip=1, header=T)
df2 <- read.csv( "Data Files/Study 1 - Raw Data - Deidentified.csv")
names(df) <- names(df2)
df <- df[-1,]

# Create Subject ID
df$ID <- as.factor(1:nrow(df))

# Read Age file
age.values <- read.csv("Data Files/Study 1 - Age.csv", header=F)
age.values <- unlist(age.values)
```


# Data Exclusion

To exclude participants who incorrectly recalled their version choice.
```{r}
df$Recall_Correct <- as.character(df$Game_Choice) == as.character(df$Recall)

#Frequency table
table(df$Recall_Correct)

#Perentage who passed comprehension checks
sum(df$Recall_Correct==TRUE) / ( sum(df$Recall_Correct==TRUE, df$Recall_Correct==FALSE)) *100

#Drop cases who failed comprehension checks
df <- df[df$Recall_Correct == 1,]
```

# Data Preparation

### Version Choice
```{r}
# Recode such that 0 = No pain (Version A), 1 = Pain (Version B)
df$Game_Choice_Binary <- NA
df$Game_Choice_Binary[df$Game_Choice == 1] <- 0
df$Game_Choice_Binary[df$Game_Choice == 2] <- 1

df$Game_Choice_Binary <- as.factor(df$Game_Choice_Binary)

# Frequency Distribution Table 
table(df$Game_Choice_Binary)
```

### Platform used for Finger Agility
```{r}
# Compute variable 'Platform' and label its levels
df$Platform <- factor(df$Platform, 
                      levels = c(1,2,3,4),
                      labels = c("trackpad", "mouse", "touch screen", "other"))

# Frequencies
table(df$Platform)

# Show 'Other' responses
table(df$Platform_4_TEXT)
```

### Pain score 
Due to mistake in Qualtrics (two '1': 1 1 2 3 4 5 6 7), I analyse it in two ways
1) Treat both '1's as '1'
2) Treat it as a 8-point scale (i.e., 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8)

#### Approach #1
(both '1s' as '1s)
```{r}
# Compute / redo variable
df$Pain1 <- as.numeric(as.character(df$Pain))
df$Pain1[df$Pain1 == 8] <- 1

table(df$Pain1)
# Descriptives: Pain - Grand mean
describe(df$Pain1)

# Descriptives: Pain by choice (versions A vs. B)
describeBy(df$Pain1, group = df$Game_Choice_Binary)

# t-test
t.test(df$Pain1 ~ df$Game_Choice_Binary)
```

#### Approach #2
(as 8-point scale)
```{r}
# Compute / redo variable
df$Pain2 <- NULL
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 1] <- 1
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 8] <- 2
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 2] <- 3
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 3] <- 4
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 4] <- 5
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 5] <- 6
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 6] <- 7
df$Pain2[df$Pain == 7] <- 8

table(df$Pain2)

# Descriptives: Pain - Grand mean
describe(df$Pain2)

# Descriptives: Pain by choice (versions A vs. B)
describeBy(df$Pain2, group = df$Game_Choice_Binary)

# t-test
t.test(df$Pain2 ~ df$Game_Choice_Binary)
```

# Wide to Long Conversion (for mixed ANOVA)
'df.long' is the 'long' dataframe
```{r}
df.long <- gather(df, time, likelihood, c("Likelihood1", "Likelihood2", "Likelihood3"))
```

# Mixed ANOVA (T1 vs T2)
```{r}
aov_time_choice <- aov(likelihood ~ Game_Choice_Binary*time + Error(ID/time), 
                       data=df.long[(df.long$time == "Likelihood1" | df.long$time == "Likelihood2"),])
summary(aov_time_choice)

model.tables(aov_time_choice, "means")
```

# Paired sample t-test
Change across time for each between-subject group
```{r}
Mixed_Fitted_Interaction<-emmeans(aov_time_choice, ~time|as.factor(Game_Choice_Binary))
Mixed_Fitted_Interaction
pairs(Mixed_Fitted_Interaction)
```

# Assumption check for Mixed ANOVA (T1 vs T2)
```{r}
# Assumption check: Levene's test
leveneTest(likelihood~ time*Game_Choice_Binary, data=df.long[(df.long$time == "Likelihood1" | df.long$time == "Likelihood2"),], center=median)

# Robust ANOVA with 10% trim rate
### Interaction term remains significant

mixed_anova_rob1 <- bwtrim(formula = likelihood ~ Game_Choice_Binary*time, id = ID, 
       data = df.long[(df.long$time == "Likelihood1" | df.long$time == "Likelihood2"),], tr = 0.1)
mixed_anova_rob1
```

# Mixed ANOVA (T1 vs T3)
```{r}
leveneTest(likelihood~ time*Game_Choice_Binary, data=df.long[(df.long$time == "Likelihood1" | df.long$time == "Likelihood3"),], center=median)

aov_time_choice <- aov(likelihood ~ Game_Choice_Binary*time + Error(ID/time), 
                       data=df.long[(df.long$time == "Likelihood1" | df.long$time == "Likelihood3"),])
summary(aov_time_choice)

model.tables(aov_time_choice, "means")
```

# Assumption check for Mixed ANOVA (T1 vs T3)
```{r}
# Assumption check: Levene's test
leveneTest(likelihood~ time*Game_Choice_Binary, data=df.long[(df.long$time == "Likelihood1" | df.long$time == "Likelihood3"),], center=median)

# Robust ANOVA with 10% trim rate
### Interaction term remains significant

mixed_anova_rob2 <- bwtrim(formula = likelihood ~ Game_Choice_Binary*time, id = ID, 
       data = df.long[(df.long$time == "Likelihood1" | df.long$time == "Likelihood3"),], tr = 0.1)
mixed_anova_rob2
```



# Plot: Likelihood x Time x Version Choice
```{r}
ggplot(df.long, aes(x = time, y = likelihood))  +
    geom_point(stat = "summary", fun.y="mean", aes(colour = Game_Choice_Binary), shape=18, size = 5) + 
  scale_color_manual(values=c("blue4", "red3"), name = "Version Choice", labels = c("No Pain", "Pain")) +
  labs(title= "Perceived Likelihood of Winning Lottery by Time and Version Choice", 
       x = "Time", y = "Perceived Likelihood of Winning Lottery") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("Time #1", "Time #2", "Time #3"))
```
